title: Waldorf Salad
subtitle: apple, celery, walnut, and mayonnaise dressing
excerpt: The Waldorf salad was created at the Waldorf hotel in New York in the 1890s. The original was just apple, celery, and mayonnaise. Walnuts were added later and became standard. This version keeps the classic combination with a lightly creamy dressing.
sourceNotes: Created at the Waldorf Hotel in New York around 1893 by matre d' Oscar Tschirky. Walnuts were added to the recipe in the early 20th century and are now considered part of the classic.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dress up to 1 hour ahead. The apple will discolour if dressed much further in advance.

content.text: Toss the apple in lemon juice as soon as it is cut to stop it browning. Use a crisp, slightly tart apple such as Granny Smith or Cox for the best flavour.

items.prepNote: use 2 eating apples, cored and diced
use a mixture of radicchio and romaine leaves

content.text: Dice the apple and toss with half the lemon juice.
Mix the mayonnaise, soured cream, remaining lemon juice, and honey in a bowl. Season with salt.
Add the apple, celery, and walnuts to the dressing. Toss gently to coat.
Arrange the salad leaves on plates. Spoon the Waldorf mixture on top. Serve chilled.

items.cause: Not tossed in lemon juice quickly enough
items.fix: Add lemon juice immediately after cutting the apple.
Thin with extra lemon juice or a splash of water.

content.text: The Waldorf salad was created at New York's Waldorf Hotel in the 1890s. Oscar Tschirky, the maitre d' who developed it, kept it simple: just apple, celery, and mayonnaise. Walnuts were added in later decades and became inseparable from the dish. It remains one of the most recognisable American salads, served everywhere from cafes to fine dining rooms.
